name: Hinduja Global Solutions Ltd
title: Hinduja Global Solutions Ltd - 532859 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: HGS FY26 revenue from operations flat at Rs 4,307 crore with EBITDA Rs 649 crore (13.4%); Q4 EBITDA margin 15.7% and 79 new client signings.
summary.overview: Management described FY26 as a year of disciplined transformation, with revenue held back by client runoffs that it calls non-recurring. Cost actions across real estate, technology and infrastructure delivered about 200 bps of margin improvement, and Q4 showed sequential recovery in revenue and margin. The Media (broadband, DTV, CelerityX) business remains loss-making at Rs 175 crore for the year, with a Rs 50 crore loss in the latest quarter. A final dividend of Rs 5 per share was recommended, and management said net treasury and cash surplus was about Rs 5,346 crore.

financial_highlights.change: Sequential expansion cited; no YoY figure stated

financial_highlights.value: Rs 5 per equity share (Rs 10 par), subject to AGM approval
financial_highlights.change: Company could not declare dividend last year

financial_highlights.value: Rs (160) crore; basic EPS of -34.52 (per investor question)

segments.name: CX / BPM (core)
segments.commentary: Contributed 55% of FY26 operating revenue and 58% in Q4. Management says the core business is stable when adjusted for runoffs.

segments.name: Digital and Media services
segments.commentary: Contributed 45% of FY26 operating revenue and 42% in Q4, with mix shifting toward digital, data, AI and platform work.

segments.name: Media (broadband, DTV, CelerityX)
segments.commentary: Loss of Rs 50 crore in Q4 and Rs 175 crore for FY26 per investor question, not disputed by management. DTV churn was about 0.62% at end-Q4 and ARPU stable at Rs 122; retail bandwidth cost fell to 26% of revenue from 28%. CelerityX enterprise revenue doubled and TCV rose 5x.

guidance_outlook: Management describes FY27 as a rebuild year, with the 79 new signings expected to ramp and AI assistants to move from pilots to production.
Some further cost impact from cost actions is expected to flow through in H1 FY27.
Management is 'cautiously optimistic', expecting steady improvement in growth and margins over time, with no numeric guidance given.
Management expects the Media losses to narrow through revenue optimisation and cost actions, including Project Ganga, but gave no timeline; it will share traction at end-Q2 FY27.
capex_capacity: Project Ganga (Uttar Pradesh): MoU signed March 9, 2026 to enable up to 10,000 Digital Service Providers and connect over 2 million households in 2 to 3 years; management says capex is funded by the state's CM Yuva Scheme loans of up to Rs 5 lakh per DSP, with HGS acting as ISP/knowledge partner.
Digital skilling MoU with UP government to skill 100,000 youth; kickoff has started.
Capex and investments in AI-led centres of excellence, package solutions, broadband and CelerityX were funded from internal cash in FY26, per management.
Headcount of almost 18,000 people cited as part of the Realized AI model.
demand_pricing: 79 new clients signed across BPM and Digital in FY26, described as the strongest year on new logos; pipeline quality described as improved and more outcome-led.
AgentX has 23 active customers and 21 AI assistants in production; eight new packaged solutions launched, including AMLens, LoanFlow and KYCVision.
Revenue by origination: India 38%, US 28%, UK 13%, others about 5% (remaining Europe and APAC not itemised in call).
Vertical mix: Tech, Media and Telecom 50%, BFSI 18%, Retail 17%, Public Sector 8%.
Delivery mix: India 42%, US 19%, US+Canada+UK about 28%, Philippines about 13% (public sector delivery stated as from Philippines, with UK 10%).
NPS at 60 with 68% promoters, described as top quartile of the industry.
Broadband mix: 15% of users on plans above 100 Mbps (from 10.7% a year earlier); 38% on 51-100 Mbps (from 31%).

qa_highlights.question: What are the four use cases of DaVinci and how does it complement the AI offerings?
qa_highlights.answer: DaVinci is a centralised data lake of customer interaction data (calls, chats, emails, transcripts). Use cases are interaction insights, identifying automatable interactions, a 360-degree customer view for agents, and operational stress-point visibility.

qa_highlights.question: Are there similar public sector deployments after the UK social care case study?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is working with multiple UK and Canadian public sector agencies and is seeing early needs in the US.

qa_highlights.question: Why declare a dividend while capex is planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY26 showed improved profitability, there is enough cash, and the dividend shares value with shareholders; it was not declared last year.

qa_highlights.question: What steps will reduce Media division losses, and does Project Ganga add to profit?
qa_highlights.answer: Levers are CelerityX enterprise growth, product mix shift to higher bandwidth, bandwidth cost negotiations with telcos, DTV content cost negotiations, and G&A cuts. Project Ganga capex is funded by the state scheme, so HGS invests mainly expertise; management gave no timeline and will update at end-Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Focus on return on capital employed given book value of about Rs 1,700 per share against a market price near Rs 400.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will look into capital efficiency and reiterated focus on capital efficiency without giving numbers.

qa_highlights.question: Status of GAAR-related income tax case on the NXTDIGITAL merger, and the negative EPS of -34.52.
qa_highlights.answer: The GAAR panel direction is under appeal at Bombay High Court, next hearing June 12, 2026. Standalone FY26 earnings were Rs (160) crore, which drives the negative EPS; management expects this to reverse as investments mature.

risks_watch: Media division losses (Rs 175 crore FY26) and continued linear TV/DTV subscriber decline; whether the Q2 FY27 update shows narrowing losses.
Revenue flat at Rs 4,307 crore; conversion of 79 new signings into revenue as they ramp in FY27.
GAAR-related tax case on the NXTDIGITAL merger; Bombay High Court hearing on June 12, 2026.
Negative standalone EPS (-34.52) and whether the Rs 5 dividend is sustained.
Return on capital employed; management did not give targets despite a Rs 1,700 book value per share versus a Rs 400 market price per investor question.
Cost actions still flowing into H1 FY27.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the operating turnaround, cost discipline and new-logo wins, but cautious on near-term revenue and the Media business. Management avoided quantifying Media loss reduction timelines and deferred timing questions to Q2 FY27.
key_quotes: FY2026 has been our strongest year ever, with 79 new clients signed on across BPM and Digital services.
I want to reiterate here that runoffs that we had in FY2026 are non-recurring in nature.
Today, our NPS is at 60, up 12.0 a year, and 68% of our clients are promoters.
Q4 has been the first signal of stabilization.

adds.what: Project Ganga (Uttar Pradesh) enabling up to 10,000 Digital Service Providers and connecting over 2 million households

growth.why: Management gave no numeric FY27 growth guidance, only "steady improvements in growth and margins over time," backed by 79 new signings, AgentX production deployments and cost actions, with no specific capacity or order numbers attached; FY26 revenue was flat at Rs 4,307 crore and Q4 YoY growth was not stated.
